actor: Unknown (GTIG describes the six-hour campaign without naming an actor; it separately tracks UNC6780 / TeamPCP for supply-chain activity)
impact: Per GTIG: a mass credential-harvesting campaign planned, built and executed in under six hours after a cloud-resource compromise; multi-agent frameworks autonomously managing scanning and credential harvesting at scale; theft of AI API credentials and co-opting of victim cloud environments for unauthorized AI workloads.
mitigations: GTIG frames enterprise AI assets (model weights, API credentials, cloud compute quotas) as high-value targets and highlights illicit account procurement and LLMJacking; it recommends defensive use of AI and secure-AI practices.
name: GTIG: adversaries ran an agent-enabled mass credential-harvesting campaign in under six hours

sources.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: From Prompting to Autonomy - The Evolution of Adversarial AI

summary: In its September 2026 AI Threat Tracker, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reported that in the second quarter of 2026 it observed threat actors compromise a cloud resource and then plan, build and execute an agent-enabled mass credential-harvesting campaign in under six hours, compressing the window defenders have to respond. GTIG describes a broader shift in which adversaries deploy multi-agent frameworks that autonomously manage scanning pipelines, resolve operational errors and execute credential harvesting at scale, and separately tracks the financially motivated group UNC6780 (TeamPCP) conducting large-scale open-source supply-chain compromises across PyPI, npm and Docker Hub since March 2026, and adversaries stealing AI API credentials and co-opting victim cloud environments to run unauthorized AI workloads. GTIG names no specific model for the six-hour campaign and no victim; it frames the activity as part of a general evolution from prompting to agentic AI.
